title: ICE cotton futures rise for third straight session on weaker dollar
summary:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled at 81.83 cents, up 1.17 per cent, its highest close since September 28, as a weaker US dollar and buying interest supported prices.
Trading volume jumped about 48 per cent to 57,445 contracts, while deliverable stocks stayed at 16,618 bales.
A faster US harvest and caution before USDA export sales data and the Federal Reserve meeting may limit gains.

title: Heimtextil 2027 to spotlight design trends at expanded Trend Space
summary:
Heimtextil 2027’s Alcova-curated Trend Space will showcase material experimentation, emerging design and three colour worlds in Frankfurt on January 12–15.
Highlights include Patricia Urquiola’s expanded three-piece Bambi family and a New Talent Area featuring over 30 newcomers.
Trends 27/28 will explore technology, functionality and tactile experiences through contrasting cool and warm palettes.

title: Bangladesh plans trade licence portal & joint inspections
summary:
Bangladesh plans to issue trade licences through a single online portal and combine regulatory inspections to cut delays, duplication and compliance costs for businesses. 
Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said firms would apply, upload documents, pay fees and receive licences remotely. 
The task force is also considering longer licence validity and easier foreign work permit renewals.

title: UK's CBI urges Chancellor to cut business costs in Autumn Budget
summary:
The CBI has urged the UK Chancellor to use the Autumn Budget to give firms breathing space, cut costs and unlock private investment.
Its submission seeks lower non-domestic electricity costs from April 2027, a £1,000 (~$1,333) rise in the employer National Insurance threshold and business rates reform.
It also proposes AI adoption and delivery measures.

title: The future of fabric is smart, and brands must price it right
summary:
Smart textiles are opening opportunities for apparel brands as consumers seek activity monitoring, temperature regulation and health insights.
Fortune Business Insights values the global market at $2.43 billion in 2025 and $8.48 billion by 2034; IMARC sees India at $957.5 million.
Sportswear and healthcare may lead adoption, but cost, durability, scaling and data privacy remain barriers.

title: Taiwan's Fulgent Sun's Q3 revenue rises 42%
summary:
Taiwanese footwear OEM Fulgent Sun’s FY26 Q3 revenue rose 42.32 per cent year on year to NT$5.44 billion (~$167.84 million), supported by added capacity. 
Operating profit fell 23.74 per cent and net income attributable to owners dropped 54.68 per cent despite higher gross profit. 
Margins narrowed on tariffs, raw-material volatility, wage rises, start-up costs at new plants and foreign-exchange impact.

title: US' UniFirst FY26 revenue rises as merger costs curb profit
summary:
UniFirst Corporation recorded fiscal 2026 revenue of $2.52 billion, up 3.7 per cent, supported by growth across its operating segments. 
Net income fell to $109.5 million as proposed Cintas merger and enterprise resource planning costs weighed on earnings. 
Fourth-quarter revenue rose 5 per cent to $645 million, while adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 14.7 per cent.

title: US apparel imports from Peru fall 10.4% as supplier trends diverge
summary:
Peruvian exporters must factor a 12.5 per cent US Section 301 duty into covered US-bound apparel shipments, as Peru’s free-trade agreement does not remove the new charge.
US exemptions apply only to qualifying USMCA and CAFTA-DR textile and apparel entries.
US apparel imports fell 7.4 per cent to about $49.08 billion in January-August 2026, with supplier performance diverging.

title: From online hype to profit: Why India’s apparel brands need stores
summary:
India’s D2C apparel websites account for only $3.3 billion, or 3.4 per cent, of the country’s $95.7 billion domestic apparel market in 2025.
Offline channels still hold 83 per cent of sales, while marketplaces take about 80 per cent of online apparel sales, CMAI and 1Lattice found.
Rahul Mehta says brands need customer data, stores and profitability as consolidation looms.

title: Germany's Adidas raises 2026 profit outlook to $2.81 bn
summary:
Adidas raised its 2026 operating profit outlook to €2.5 billion (~$2.81 billion) after record Q3 results.
Revenue rose 9 per cent to €7.252 billion (~$8.14 billion), while operating profit climbed 37 per cent to €1.008 billion (~$1.13 billion). 
Full-price sales and a US tariff refund supported margins, with fourth-quarter investment planned to strengthen future profitability.

title: New Zealand's apparel imports rise 5.9% in September 2026
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports rose 5.9 per cent year on year to NZ$190.20 million ($107.85 million) in September, a third straight monthly gain.
January–September imports were virtually flat at NZ$1.567 billion, with knitted apparel up 0.7 per cent and non-knitted down 0.8 per cent.
Exports fell 2.6 per cent to NZ$18.52 million in September, as knitted apparel shipments dropped but non-knitted exports rose.

title: Luxury’s split market: Ultra-rich spend, aspirational buyers retreat
summary:
Global luxury fashion revenue fell 0.5 per cent in 2025 and is forecast to grow 2.2 per cent in 2026, with growth tapering towards 2031 as aspirational buyers curb spending.
LVMH led luxury goods in 2025 with a 21 per cent share; fashion held 29 per cent, behind watches and jewellery at 34 per cent.
US 2026 revenue is estimated at $96.9 billion, ahead of China at $92.7 billion.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to EU may gain in late 2026: Eurostat
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU could regain momentum late in 2026 and in 2027 as the bloc’s import decline narrows, according to the Eurostat data. 
EU apparel imports fell 3.83 per cent to €60.29 billion (~$67.74 billion) in January-August; Bangladesh’s shipments dropped 11.67 per cent to €11.93 billion (~$13.40 billion). 
August EU import value rose 0.72 per cent year on year.

title: France's Damartex protects profitability amid Q1 revenue decline
summary:
French apparel group Damartex reported an 8 per cent revenue decline to €98.6 million (~$110.68 million) in Q1 FY27 amid hot weather and weak consumer confidence. 
Fashion sales fell as seasonal purchases were delayed, while home and healthcare businesses also declined. 
The group prioritised profitability and operational discipline without disclosing quarterly profit or margin figures.

title: India’s athleisure trend is growing, but sportswear is just 1%
summary:
India’s apparel market is valued at $95.7 billion in 2025, but sportswear holds only about 1 per cent despite athleisure hype and growth expectations.
CMAI-1Lattice data shows men lead sportswear at $630 million, ahead of kids at $250 million and women at $150 million.
Among men, 17 per cent of track pant or suit buyers bought online, while major offline chains already stock the category.
